Despite the hit-or-miss dishes, I’d definitely swing by Wicked Wolf again. That chicken sandwich is worth a return visit, and I'm keen to try some other items on the menu. If you're in the area, give it a shot—just maybe skip the Scarpariello!

My culinary quest led me to San Gennaro on Arthur Avenue, which is a charming, small spot in the heart of the Bronx's Little Italy—a great location for a weekend brunch or afternoon espresso.

Unfortunately, my experience with both the quality of the food quality and service was sadly disappointing.

For appetizers, I ordered the Burrata and Calamari Fritti, (both were very nice)followed by the server-recommended main, the Paccheri Genovese. Despite only one other table being seated, the main course took approximately 30 minutes to arrive and was delivered at roughly room temperature. While the meat in the dish was well-cooked, the accompanying sauce lacked any distinct flavor to activate the dish.

Even granting grace that this may have been an off day for the staff, the combination of the significant wait time, the lukewarm food, and the overall poor service prevents me from recommending this restaurant.

We go down to Arthur Ave for dinner from time to time and always like to try a new place.
Tonight we decided on Tra Di Noi.
It's on 187th street around the corner from Arthur Ave.
The restaurant is small and cozy and has the old school Italian restaurant  red checkered table cloths.
We were greeted warmly by the hostess and seated at table against the wall in the dining Area. The table had salt, pepper, bread dishes, utensil set ups with a napkin and an olive oil bottle.
A waiter came over and explained the specials to us and took out drink order. The waiter then brought us bread and water to start. They only have beer and wine and I asked for a non alcoholic beer but they don't serve it.
The menu is small but has something for everyone and the specials more than make up for the smaller size menu.
We ordered fried calamari and a mussels special for the appetizers.
The calamari was ok. It was fried a little harder then I like but it was a nice size for 2 people and came with tubes and baby octopus. The Marinara with it was a little bland for my taste.
The mussels in white wine appetizer was fantastic and a great portion.
For the entree we had an order of the pork chop with vinegar peppers specials and a rigatoni special.
Both entrees were delicious and they came with a small plate of fingerling potatoes and string beans that were nicely sauteed with garlic and oil.
We split a piece of homemade Italian cheesecake and I had an espresso and both were absolutely delicious.
The staff was friendly and knowledgeable and attentive. The waiter came by and offered us more bread which a lot of places dont do.

This is a real Italian restaurant owned and operated by real Italians which is something that is hard to come by these days in the Italian restaurant business.
The food is as close to homemade as you can get.
It's not mass produced so you are not going to get heaping portions like you may get in other places but what you do get is a dish that is crafted with care to be as authentic as possible.
The restaurant is quiant and cozy and is staffed by friendly people.
We left the restaurant happy and you will as well.

I stopped by here completely on a whim, and I'm so glad I did! The food is absolutely fantastic—packed with flavor without being overly salty. Everything I've tried has been delicious, which is why I've come back several times since my first visit.

I was really excited to try this place after seeing so many TikTok reviews, but unfortunately, it didn’t live up to the hype.

The restaurant itself is small, which I don’t mind, but there was live music playing at an extremely loud volume. It made it difficult to hear our server, and she couldn’t hear us either. The service was just okay. The hostess was friendly, but the wait was about 45 minutes. Our waitress didn’t check in on us after the food was served, which was disappointing because I would’ve mentioned that my chuleta seemed over-fried in old oil, it even had a puddle of oil on it. We also ordered wings as an appetizer, and they came out lukewarm and soggy.

On a positive note, the bistec and arroz con gandules were both very good.

Overall, the experience wasn’t worth the 1 hour and 45 minute drive. I had high hopes, but left disappointed.

The highlight was the Mixed Grill plate which has all of the famous grilled meats and sausages, along with some cheese and more roasted potatoes. I cannot explain the scope of flavor in each type of meat on the plate, as you should treat yourself and anyone willing to all that it offers. The wait staff was phenomenal and courteous, treating my wife as the only woman there, as well as lady should be and serving her. The food does take a bit longer than you may be used to but it’s because of how fresh it is. You owe it to yourself to go and try this place, as it was exquisite experience and I cannot wait to go back.

I attended a family celebration at this steakhouse over the weekend for my aunt’s 70th birthday. My family had reserved a large table, and when I arrived, there wasn’t an available seat yet. I simply went to the bar area intending to order food and a drink while waiting.

Before I could even speak with the bartender, a man who later appeared to be the manager immediately approached me in a rude and confrontational manner about seats at the bar that had drinks sitting there but no people present. I calmly explained that I only needed a place to sit briefly while ordering and that I would gladly move once the guests returned.

What made the situation extremely uncomfortable was that he repeatedly tapped me while speaking to me. I politely told him to stop touching me because it was inappropriate and intimidating. Instead of handling the situation professionally, he became louder and increasingly disrespectful.

If this person was truly the manager, his behavior reflected a complete lack of professionalism, customer service, and respect especially toward a woman who was simply trying to order food and enjoy a family event peacefully. Managers are supposed to de-escalate situations, introduce themselves professionally, and treat guests with courtesy. Unfortunately, that was not my experience here at all.

The atmosphere and overall experience left such a negative impression on me that I would never personally return or spend my money there again. The only reason I stayed briefly was because my cousin encouraged me not to leave during our family celebration.

I frequent many upscale establishments throughout New York and New Jersey and have encountered countless managers and hospitality professionals over the years. This experience stood out for all the wrong reasons. Respect and professionalism cost nothing, and unfortunately, neither was shown that evening.

Thank you to everyone at the Morris Park Inn for your incredible hospitality. Love, community, and kindness are what truly make America great.

text.text: We had lunch at Orrico's today, following Wally's Instagram testimonial! It did not disappoint! Toni Ann and Robert are the most warm and friendly owners/host and chef! There were four of us, and we ordered a bunch of appetizers to start, one more delicious than the next! Baked clams oreganato were perfectly seasoned and fresh. If you can imagine a potato croquette getting any better, these were smothered in the most delicious marsala mushroom sauce. Dirty potato chips… Smothered in Gorgonzola sauce with chopped tomato and meatball! Delicious creamy arancini...the tomato sauce is amazing. For entrées, we were actually stuffed and decided to share a few entrées. We went with the highly recommended chicken parm and a custom dish that chef Robert was happy to oblige on! It was fried eggplant layered with a brown marsala mushroom sauce and melted mozzarella cheese. To die for!  We had the spinach salad with cranberries, pears, and candied walnuts, and a raspberry vinegar dressing.... Side of bleu cheese. Amazing. The portions are so generous, we actually took leftovers home! Not that we needed it, but the delicious fresh crusty bread brought to the table, hit the spot as well, especially when soaking up all of the delicious sauces from our dishes! Quick ride from Westchester for sure! We will most definitely be back! Thanks so much from Bobby, Pat, Laura and Lisa!!
